lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ricardo Wertheim | Lesson 15 -- Have You Ever...?
lesson.grammar_point: present perfect for life experiences (have you ever, never, been to) contrasted with past simple for finished time

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: happy to try new and exciting things
to take something off a list because you did it
so special that it happens only one time in your life
something that happens to you and stays with you
to feel sorry about something you did, or did not do
a list of things you want to do before you die
to try something new, to see if you like it
the best or most exciting part of a trip or an event

items.situation: Ask me about one country I have visited. Use ever.
tips: Yes, I have / No, I haven't

items.situation: Tell me one food you have never tried, and if you want to try it.
Say one thing that is still on your bucket list.
tips: It is on my bucket list

items.situation: Tell me the highlight of your trip to Croatia, and WHEN it happened.
Say something you have done many times in your life as an architect.
Tell a friend about one thing you regret not doing on a trip.

listenings.text: When I turned seventy, my daughter gave me a small notebook and said: Dad, write your bucket list. I laughed, but I did it. Now, three years later, I have crossed off six things. I have seen the northern lights in Norway. I have taken a cooking class in Bologna. I have even ridden a horse, for the first time in my life, at seventy-one. But I have never been to Japan, and that is still at the top of the list. People sometimes ask me: Aren't you too old for this? I always give the same answer. I don't regret the things I did. I only regret the things I never tried.

I work as a tour guide in Ljubljana, and every week a tourist asks me the same question: Have you ever eaten anything strange here? The honest answer is yes. I have eaten a horse burger, which is a local favorite, and I have tried cheese with honey and black pepper. I was not very adventurous as a child, but this job has changed me. My rule now is simple. If a local recommends something, I give it a try. Most of the time it is delicious. Once, it was terrible. But even that terrible dinner is a good story now, and I have told it maybe a hundred times. That is the real highlight of traveling. You don't collect photos. You collect experiences.

extra_audio.text: First Elena asked him at breakfast: Have you ever swum in the sea at night? Then he said no, he was not very adventurous after dark, and they both laughed. After that he walked the city walls and crossed one more thing off his list. At that point, at ten o'clock, Elena took him to a little beach under the walls. In the end he swam for twenty minutes, and it was the highlight of the whole trip.
